title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles were left stationary on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations after their batteries drained while the cars were stuck in severe traffic. At least a dozen vehicles, mostly Jaguar I-PACE models, remained immobilized near the Golden Gate Bridge following fireworks displays. The company attributed the stranding to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unexpected road closures.

This reveals a system deployed without adequate safeguards for edge cases. The vehicles lacked either sufficient battery capacity for foreseeable event-related congestion, mechanisms to route around predicted gridlock, or fallback protocols to move themselves to safer locations when stationary. Catching this would have required stress-testing the autonomous system under conditions known to occur in San Francisco during major public events, or constraining operations when such events were forecast.

It is not established whether the fire that occurred when a vehicle drove over fireworks resulted from a system failure or from circumstances the autonomous driving system could not be expected to prevent.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Several Waymo autonomous vehicles were stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations after their batteries depleted while stuck in severe traffic. Video footage showed at least a dozen Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up stationary following fireworks displays near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unexpected road closures. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported. Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles from roadways.

The incident caused significant frustration among stranded motorists, with some spending nearly two hours in standstill traffic. Residents expressed anger at the stationary autonomous vehicles blocking roads with no drivers present. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the traffic situation with stakeholders to improve future event management. This marks another challenge for Waymo in San Francisco, following a previous service pause in December when a power outage affected traffic lights and caused some autonomous vehicles to stall at intersections.
